subject: general
question: If a lit candle is covered with a glass tumbler, the flame gets extinguished after some time. What is the reason for this?

options.text: Due to limited oxygen the covered candle got extinguished after some time.
Due to limited carbon dioxide the covered candle got extinguished after some time.
Due to limited sulphur the covered candle got extinguished after some time.
Due to limited nitrogen the covered candle got extinguished after some time.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Due to limited oxygen the covered candle got extinguished after some time.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Oxygen** is essential for **combustion**. When a lit candle is covered with a glass tumbler, the **oxygen inside the tumbler is gradually consumed by the flame**.
 
• As the oxygen level **decreases**, the** flame's ability to sustain combustion diminishes**.
 
• Eventually, the oxygen level drops below the required threshold to support the flame, causing the candle to extinguish.
 
• This process demonstrates the principle that a **continuous supply of oxygen is necessary for maintaining combustion**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Combustion is a chemical reaction that typically involves the **rapid combination of a fuel with oxygen, producing heat and light**.
 
• The flame of a candle is a result of the combustion of the wax, which is the fuel, in the presence of oxygen from the air.
 
• In an enclosed space, once the available oxygen is depleted, combustion cannot continue, leading to the extinguishment of the flame.
 
• This principle is also why fire safety protocols emphasize the importance of controlling oxygen availability to manage and extinguish fires.
